raw_case_text:
A 54-year-old woman with a history of breast cancer, which was in remission, and porphyria cutanea tarda complicated by iron overload, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma, underwent liver transplantation. The liver was donated by a kidney transplant recipient who died of suspected cytomegalovirus (CMV) encephalitis. During postoperative care, the patient received prophylactic ganciclovir for CMV and fluconazole (FLC) for Candida spp. She was discharged with an undetectable blood CMV viral load. One month later, the patient received high-dose glucocorticoid therapy for the treatment of acute rejection (confirmed by histological analysis of the graft) and was maintained on tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisone (10 mg/day). Four days later, she was readmitted to the hospital due to fever, headache, and vomiting. Upon physical examination, the patient was conscious, alert, and had no neurological abnormalities. A head computed tomography (CT) scan was performed and revealed no abnormalities. Subsequently, a lumbar puncture was performed. The opening pressure was 30 cmH2O. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis revealed neutrophilic pleocytosis (112 leukocytes/mm3, neutrophils 66%), elevated protein (320 mg/dL) and lactate (7.2 mmol/L) levels, and very low glucose (3 mg/dL) levels. Rare, encapsulated yeast cells consistent with Cryptococcus spp. were observed on nigrosin-stained direct microscopic examination of the CSF (quantification: 0.1 yeasts/microL) and the cryptococcal antigen lateral flow assay (CrAg LFA; Immuno-Mycologics; IMMY; Norman, OK) yielded a positive result. Induction therapy with amphotericin B (AmB) deoxycholate (50 mg/day) and high-dose FLC (800 mg/day) was initiated. Cryptococcus spp. were cultured from CSF after 6 days of incubation and identified as belonging to the C. gattii complex using matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS) (Bruker Daltonics, Billerica, MA, USA). The isolate was then subjected to multilocus sequence typing (MLST). The nuclear loci CAP59, GPD1, IGS1, LAC1, PLB1, SOD1, and URA5 were amplified and sequenced as previously described. The isolate was identified as C. deuterogattii and deposited in the Microbiological Collections of Parana Network (CMRP-Taxonline) CMRP6193 (Figure 1). The newly generated sequence has been deposited in the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) GenBank nucleotide database (PQ467994 to PQ467999).
On the 11th day of antifungal therapy, AmB was discontinued owing to the occurrence of renal toxicity, and high-dose FLC was continued as monotherapy. Follow-up CSF cultures revealed no fungal growth after the 13th day of treatment. Multiple therapeutic lumbar punctures were performed to control the intracranial pressure. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the head revealed T2/FLAIR hyperintensities at the surface of the brain, cerebellar gyri, brainstem, ependyma and white matter, as well as leptomeningeal contrast enhancement (Figure 2). Chest CT performed to rule out pulmonary involvement revealed no signs of lung disease. The patient completed 8 weeks of antifungal therapy during hospitalization and received a 3-week course of intravenous ganciclovir due to the detectable CMV DNA in the CSF. Shortly after a diagnosis of cryptococcosis was made, a review of the donor's cultures conducted at the originating institution revealed that Cryptococcus spp. had been identified in blood cultures, a result that was unavailable at transplantation. Due to persistent immunosuppression associated with treatment using everolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisone (5 mg/day), maintenance therapy with FLC (300 mg/day) was prescribed indefinitely. After 5 years of follow-up, the patient experienced no relapse of cryptococcal or CMV disease and showed no considerable sequelae.
The patient's written consent for publication was obtained prior to data collection and making of this paper. This research has been approved by Hospital de Clinicas Federal University of Parana Ethics Committee (research number 71396723.9.0000.0096).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 54-year-old female recent liver transplant recipient presented with acute fever, headache, and vomiting.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Approximately 1 month after undergoing orthotopic liver transplantation (from a donor who died of suspected CMV encephalitis and was retrospectively found to have Cryptococcus blood culture positivity), the patient was treated with high-dose glucocorticoids for biopsy-proven acute graft rejection while on tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisone 10 mg/day. Four days after rejection therapy, she was readmitted with fever, headache, and vomiting.
subjective.past_medical_history: Orthotopic liver transplantation ~1 month prior for cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma secondary to porphyria cutanea tarda complicated by iron overload; history of breast cancer in remission; recent acute cellular graft rejection treated with high-dose corticosteroids.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, headache, and vomiting. Home medications included tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisone 10 mg/day (plus postoperative ganciclovir and fluconazole prophylaxis).

objective.physical_examination: Conscious, alert, and oriented with no focal neurological abnormalities on physical examination.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial head CT and subsequent chest CT were normal. Brain MRI revealed T2/FLAIR hyperintensities along the brain surface, cerebellar gyri, brainstem, ependyma, and white matter with leptomeningeal contrast enhancement. Lumbar puncture showed elevated opening pressure of 30 cmH2O, neutrophilic pleocytosis (112 leukocytes/mm3, 66% neutrophils), elevated protein (320 mg/dL), elevated lactate (7.2 mmol/L), and severely decreased glucose (3 mg/dL), along with detectable CMV DNA in the CSF.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis of donor-derived Cryptococcus deuterogattii (C. gattii complex) meningitis with concurrent CSF cytomegalovirus reactivation, confirmed by nigrosin direct microscopy (0.1 yeasts/uL), positive CSF cryptococcal antigen lateral flow assay (CrAg LFA), CSF culture, MALDI-TOF MS, and multilocus sequence typing (MLST; isolate CMRP6193, GenBank PQ467994-PQ467999), alongside retrospective confirmation of donor Cryptococcus fungemia. Treated with induction amphotericin B deoxycholate (50 mg/day) plus high-dose fluconazole (800 mg/day), switching to high-dose fluconazole monotherapy on day 11 due to renal toxicity (achieving negative CSF cultures after day 13 and completing 8 weeks of inpatient therapy), serial therapeutic lumbar punctures for ICP control, a 3-week course of IV ganciclovir for CSF CMV, and indefinite maintenance fluconazole (300 mg/day) while on everolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisone 5 mg/day, with no relapse over 5 years of follow-up.
